html:
The Archbishopric of Ohrid was a self governing Orthodox church based at Ohrid, set up by the Byzantine emperor Basil II in 1019 after he conquered the empire of Tsar Samuel.

Basil kept the church of the conquered Bulgarian state but placed it under a Greek archbishop. For centuries it ruled the Orthodox of much of the central Balkans, including Serbs until the Serbian church broke free in 1219. It survived the Ottoman conquest, and its cathedral of Saint Sophia, with frescoes from the 1000s, still stands. The sultan abolished it in 1767 at the request of the Patriarch of Constantinople. The Macedonian Orthodox Church of North Macedonia, founded in 1967, sees itself as its heir.
sum: The Archbishopric of Ohrid was a self governing Orthodox church based at Ohrid, set up by the Byzantine emperor Basil II in 1019 after he conquered the empire of Tsar Samuel.
